readerTitle: Two finalists, one night-shift job: who gets it?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (식품 포장·물류 센터의 야간 교대 리더 채용) + 소프트웨어 적용 노트 · 인물과 결과는 모두 설명용
insight: 두 후보를 서로 비교하지 말고, 미리 정한 일의 기준에 각각 비춰 본다. 그러면 첫인상이 아니라 그 일을 해낼 사람이 보인다.
misconception: 면접에서 가장 인상이 좋고 경력이 화려한 사람이 일도 가장 잘한다. 팀과 잘 어울릴 것 같은 느낌이 좋은 판단 근거다.

sources.text: 채용 실무의 표준 원칙 (역할 정의, 구조화 면접, 실무 과제, 평판 확인, 온보딩). 이 유닛의 PPL-03-01~06 개념 레슨과 연결
모든 인물, 회사, 결과는 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: 전체가 가상 시나리오입니다. 실제 연구 수치나 통계는 쓰지 않았습니다. 구조화 면접과 실무 과제의 효과에 대한 일반적인 서술만 있으니, 수치를 추가하려면 1차 출처를 먼저 확인하세요.
실무 과제는 유급, 짧은 시간(2시간), 익명 처리한 실제 업무 자료라는 조건으로 적었습니다. 특정 국가의 노동법상 요건은 다루지 않습니다.
5번 카드 수치 확인: 목표 4개 중 Dana 2개, Marco 4개 충족. 3번 도크 2시간 공백은 가상 설정입니다.

cards.title: Two finalists, one night-shift job: who gets it?
body: You run a food packing and distribution site. You need a night-shift lead for 30 people and six loading docks.
**Dana** spent ten years at a bigger rival. She was polished, and the interview felt like a great conversation. **Marco** started as a forklift driver and stumbled over his first answer.
Everyone already has a favorite. Over the next four decisions, you choose.

image.label: Two candidate folders on a desk in a warehouse office
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 창밖으로 야간 조명이 켜진 물류 창고가 보이는 사무실 책상 위에 이력서 폴더 두 개. 한쪽은 두껍고 반짝이는 폴더, 다른 쪽은 얇고 소박한 폴더. 실제 회사 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Before round two, what do you do first?
body: Second interviews are next week. Your managers are already saying "Dana's clearly the one."

options.text: Write down the three or four things this lead must achieve in the first six months
options.feedback: You now have a yardstick that measures both people against the job, not against each other or the first impression.

options.text: Reuse the old job ad: "10+ years' experience, strong communicator"
options.feedback: That list describes Dana's résumé, not the night shift. You'd be grading the candidates on the wrong test.

options.text: Ask the team which candidate they liked best
options.feedback: You'd learn about their impressions. But you'd have opinions with nothing to check them against.

cards.title: Say you chose A. How do you run the interviews?
body: Your list: cover no-shows without huge overtime bills, keep trucks loading on time, coach two new hires, and spot safety problems early.
Three managers will interview each finalist.

options.text: Ask both the same questions tied to the list. Each manager scores alone before anyone talks
options.feedback: The scores are close, and now you know why. Dana leads on communication and Marco leads on planning. Nobody's opinion copied anyone else's.

options.text: Keep it relaxed and conversational to see their real personality
options.feedback: Dana wins again, because a relaxed chat measures how good someone is at relaxed chats. You learn little about night shifts.

options.text: Same questions, but discuss as a group before scoring
options.feedback: Fairer questions, but the most senior voice speaks first and the scores drift toward it.

cards.title: Say you chose A. The scores are close. Now what?
body: Dana explains things clearly. Marco plans carefully. Both answers sounded good, but answers are not the work.

options.text: Give both a paid two-hour task: plan a real, anonymized shift with two no-shows and a late truck
options.feedback: You see each person do a slice of the actual job, under the same conditions. The next card shows what happened.

options.text: Pick Dana. A lead needs to communicate above all
options.feedback: Communication matters, but it was one item on your list of four. You'd be picking on the item where she shines.

options.text: Hold a third interview to break the tie
options.feedback: More talk gives you more of the same signal. It costs a week and probably leaves the tie in place.

cards.softwareNote: For a software hire, the same step is a short, paid task close to the real work, such as fixing a bug in a small sample codebase or pairing for an hour, instead of another round of puzzle questions.

cards.title: The work sample changed the picture.
body: Dana presented her plan beautifully, but dock 3 was unstaffed for two hours. Marco moved a trained picker to cover the gap and noticed that a forklift driver's certification expired that week.

breakdown.label: Dana
breakdown.detail: Strong on coaching and communication, gaps in coverage and loading

breakdown.label: Marco
breakdown.detail: Covered every dock, kept trucks on time, flagged a safety issue

cards.callout: Measured against the job, the "obvious" choice wasn't obvious anymore.
cards.softwareNote: In software, the clearest presenter and the most careful builder are often different people. Both the task and the scoring should reflect what the job needs most.

cards.title: Compare each candidate to the job, not to each other.
body: Each decision you made matches an idea from this unit: **Decision 1**, defining the role; **Decision 2**, structured interviews; **Decision 3**, testing real skills; **Decision 4**, culture add, targeted reference checks and onboarding.
**Try it today:** for the next role you hire, write down three or four things the person must achieve in six months. Then write one interview question for each.
